title: Genesis: three engine-fix follow-ups banked from the plan-review dogfood (D010/D012)
body: Drafted (NOT locked) to fix three dispatch/close/patch-completeness frictions surfaced dogfooding plan-review 2026-06-01-001: (F001) no_progress breaker too blunt — extend the convergence-bugs-v2 Design B carve-out from strictly-shrinking finding COUNT to changing finding CONTENT, so distinct per-round findings count as progress while materially-unchanged repeats still trip; (F002) make operator-finish a first-class close for honest terminals (signed-off-adjacent / staging-blocked / operator-verified) instead of a stopped_no_progress pretence, writing accurate evidence and triggering no paid dispatch; (F003) patch-completeness must surface an untracked IMPLEMENTATION module alongside an untracked test (the F007 sizing_gate.py miss) without broad noisy reporting of unrelated generated/runtime files. Intentionally small + engine-fix scoped. Sequence F001 first (it improves every later dispatch's convergence). Do NOT touch unrelated plan-review features.

title: Bootstrapping decision: build engine fixes operator-style; cross-vendor assurance from one batched audit
body: Engine fixes that repair the dispatch/close/patch-completeness machinery may be built operator-style first because running them through the affected machinery can invalidate the result. Cross-vendor assurance comes from a final batched audit, not from multi-round self-hosted dispatch. Concretely for this plan: build each feature with local TDD (red->green->refactor), do NOT run the full implement->audit volley for the build, run ONE batched codex audit at close. Precedent: D005 of 2026-06-01-001 (F009 built operator-style because lock/dispatch routed through the path it repaired) and 2026-05-30-002 convergence-bugs-v2 (closed via one batched codex audit).
